frozen.frozen_note: Pre-registration. Immutable after the P0 commit: the verifier compares this object with its copy at that commit. Moving a pillar away from a predicted IMPLEMENTED_AND_VERIFIED needs a falsification artifact in that pillar's evidence.

materiality.rule: a dedicated slice needs >= 3 % of a named weighted denominator (default KME-L weighted; CPP-D-W7 for CPP-corpus claims)
materiality.exceptions: correctness, authority, security, horizontal primitive: argued separately in the pillar's evidence; an exception never lowers the threshold for another pillar
materiality.displacement: a saving is realized only when displaced work is measured on the same denominator; otherwise it is an interval or UNKNOWN
materiality.transfer: a performance guarantee promoted to CBR needs a second, materially independent workload

KME-L.weighting: input 1 + cache_read 0.1 + cache_write 2 + output 5 (CE weighting). ESTIMATE of relative token burden, not price, not the Owner's meter.
KME-L.attribution_range: proportional attribution by KME tool-call share gives 3824.34 USD-eq over all 557 scanned local sessions; the true KME burden lies in [3824, 5850]

KME-G.note: 151 a7 sessions with zero API calls = the Login-expired relaunch loop of 2026-10-02

CPP-D-W7.note: CE frozen denominator D-W7 (CPP corpus 7 d to 2026-10-02), referenced, never re-measured here

pillars.name: mission relay in a shared checkout (worker worktree diverged from main)
pillars.rule: correctness exception. A red test first reproduces the measured hold (cwd and work_dir both carry commits); the fix relays without losing the worktree's commits and without any destructive git; PRG = a real held mission relays in the live sweep

pillars.name: remote cognitive environment integrity (GEX44 a5/a7)
pillars.rule: correctness exception. Preflight before a remote launch proves auth readiness, rules version, hook health and interpreters, or refuses with a typed reason; stale rules and broken hooks are repaired by a repeatable deploy, never hand copying; re-login itself is an Owner action

pillars.name: persistent-failure retry classification
pillars.rule: correctness exception. A worker that dies on an authorization-class failure (Login expired) parks the mission in a non-relaunching state until a qualifying precondition change; red test reproduces the 137-relaunch shape

pillars.name: silent-success hooks (per-call additional context rent)
pillars.rule: measure hook_additional_context chars per tool call on KME-L and CPP-D-W7 sessions; a slice only at >= 3 % weighted; broken hook delivery is fixed under B regardless

pillars.name: large-source read virtualization (KME heavy hitters)
pillars.rule: replay rereads of identical file versions on KME-L (same path, unchanged content between reads); build a query path in an existing owner only at >= 3 % weighted on KME-L AND confirmed on a second workload; never split source for size alone

pillars.name: GSD operational projection
pillars.rule: measure GSD workflow-doc residency (char x turns) on KME-L; if gsd-tools init already returns the compact state, hand the residency finding to the GSD owner; never fork GSD

pillars.name: derived cognition, decision and negative-result reuse with invalidation
pillars.rule: count re-tested falsified hypotheses and re-litigated sealed decisions in the corpus (positive control: listing hiding C6 -> K4); one falsifiable slice on the existing owner only if the count clears materiality or a correctness exception

pillars.name: proof reuse, singleflight, common cognitive subexpressions
pillars.rule: consume CE P and G verdicts; one KME-specific check that verification share is below materiality

pillars.name: startup floor and subagent bootstrap
pillars.rule: add the measured subagent first-call context on KME-L to CE B / SC A-C; no move of a rule or skill here

pillars.name: context lifetime, rollover, zero-transcript start, context images
pillars.rule: consume CE D, E, I; the Ralph fresh worker with an 8 KB card is the zero-transcript path

pillars.name: cognitive cost regression (startup floor ratchet)
pillars.rule: a gate that measures the current startup floor by layer and fails on a material unexplained rise versus a committed reference; a 1K universal addition reported distinctly from project-local

pillars.name: held-out efficiency benchmark, lower bound, regret
pillars.rule: offline replay of KME-L (late rollover, identical rereads, unchanged-precondition retries) ranks live experiments; live champion/challenger sessions spend quota and need an Owner decision

pillars.name: optimizer, experiment compilation, negative capital, routing, events, reality model
pillars.rule: dispositions only: CE Q/N/O/M and the pre-registration pattern of this verifier already own them; an unrestricted optimizer is rejected

pillars.name: closeout: UKDL three levels, CBR, baseline, vault, institutional GC
pillars.rule: candidates go to vault/programs/incremental-cognition/ukdl-candidates.md; promotion into ukdl-universal.md and CBR is reviewed, never silent

product.statement: A mission whose shared checkout diverged from its worker's own worktree no longer holds on the relay: the cwd alignment follows a proven worktree (a red test reproduces the earlier TypeError on proven_workstream), while the Brand #001 divergence shape stays blocked (V-MCA-DIVERGED, three-relay drill green). Verified on GEX44 (tools/test_gsd_mission_cwd_align.py 16/16); the live-sweep run on the laptop is pending.

A worker that meets an expired login (host-written refusal, zero usage) is parked as provider_held instead of being relaunched, with or without the provider breaker present, and the mission resumes by itself (provider_released, one relay) after a re-login; a budget renewal can no longer launch a fresh successor into a quarantined lineage. Built and tested on GEX44; the laptop run is pending.

One read-only command says whether an env can launch and why not (READY, NOT_READY with a reason from a closed set, or UNMEASURABLE); one command repairs a stale env by git, dry-running by default, taking the env's own lock, keeping backups and printing the rollback commands; a declared env refuses a launch on a measured NOT_READY and records the typed reasons. Today both measured envs are NOT_READY and both deploy dry-runs refuse a modified install; the Owner actions are in the bundle.

Pillars D through I can be measured on any named denominator in one scan, with a population proof first (a drifted or unobserved population is reported unmeasured, never below materiality), and the program done-gate now refuses a terminal that cites a KME-G smoke file as if it were a KME-L result, a non-reproduced primary, or a file measuring another pillar. Six tagged laptop items [D] to [I] in the owner bundle carry commands proven to parse with the instrument's own parser.

A reviewer can see the startup floor move by layer and by scope in one command: a 1,024-char addition to a universal layer goes red and is named as a universal layer, the same bytes in a project-local file are reported as project and stay green, an unexplained rise exits 1 and is cleared only by an explanation naming layer, scope, unit, a delta bound and a reason, and a comparison that could not be made exits 2 and never reads green. Smoke-proven on GEX44; the laptop reference is pending.

From one command on the laptop the Owner can see the three live experiments (late rollover, identical rereads, unchanged-precondition retries) ranked by upper bound on one named weighted denominator, each with a reading against 3 % and an unmeasured candidate listed with its reason and never shown as 0; a smoke ranking on KME-G already runs end to end on GEX44. One owner bundle opens with every Owner action, its exact command and what it closes, a gate turns red when an item or a pending check has no row, and the laptop code arrives through one guarded sync.

One command prints, for a consuming pillar, the exact owner_ledger rows the done-gate's R2 rule accepts (full 40-hex commit, terminal read from the owner ledger at that commit) or names the owner pillars still open and prints nothing pasteable; the per-pillar done-gate (--pillar) now checks R2 itself; the Owner holds two runnable bundle items, [J] and [M]. Pillars J and M are unchanged: open.

The Owner can read this run's 16 candidate learnings (6 universal, 6 domain, 4 project), each with resolving evidence refs, and the two reviews that give each one a verdict (UKDL: 4 PROMOTE-PROPOSED, 11 HOLD, 1 REJECT; CBR: none promotable); nothing was promoted, and a candidate id found in the UKDL or under vault/tower without a recorded promotion turns the closeout gate red.

intelligence.statement: On GEX44 the pillar-A gate runs 16/16, the epoch suite 82/82 and the mission suite 212/213; the one red (V-MC-PLAN-FACTS-REFUSES-OVERLAP) is a GEX44 plane fact (plan_graph_check reports node v18.19.1 outside ^22.23.2 || ^24.14.0), is not part of pillar A's hunk, and was routed to pillar B.

An auth-class refusal is classified without the breaker module by judging only host-written replies, so a model that merely quotes 'Please run /login' is not parked; a credentials rewrite after the refusal releases the park only when judged usable (unreadable or still-expired keeps it); a lineage inherits its predecessor's hold, a missing predecessor record inherits nothing, and the walk is bounded (MAX_LINEAGE_HOPS = 4).

Measured on GEX44: both measured installs are NOT_READY and predate the park and the launch gate; one install's access token is expired (expiresAt 0) and its hooks resolve into the other's tree; a lapsed access token with a live refresh token is READY with a finding, not an expired login; the installer does not copy hook scripts, so the deploy restores only registered-but-missing ones; the env node binaries (v24.15.0) are inside the vendored range and only the GEX44 main node (v18.19.1) is outside it.

KME-G smoke figures on GEX44 (never KME-L results): hook additional context is 740,326 chars over 1,105 attachments, weighted share [2.64 %, 3.96 %], so the 3 % bar sits inside the interval and the smoke cannot decide D; 142 Read results gave 0 identical rereads of any class (nothing to virtualize in this corpus; whether the harness already deduplicates cannot be told); 24 GSD doc deliveries total 175,494 chars, share [0.69 %, 1.03 %], and the one paired turn rests on a sample of one.

KME-G smoke figures on GEX44 (never KME-L results): no re-tested or re-litigated falsification record exists in the corpus (the zero means nothing to re-test here, not that re-testing does not occur); verification share is [7.30 %, 7.40 %], at or above 3 %, driven by verifier subagents, with the test-and-gate tool part only about 0.2 to 1.25 %; 11 subagent files boot at a median 125,746 tokens of first-call context (about 68 % of the main thread's first call, all cold), numerator share 8.26 %.

Measured while building the floor gate (GEX44 smoke plus one laptop probe row): the skill listing reads 30,000 chars in both GEX44 sessions (294 entries each) and in the laptop probe row (216 entries), consistent with a harness cap, an inference from three rows and not a documented limit; two same-day sessions differ by one appended 4,383-char system prompt part (a mission worker's launcher prompt), so a reference and its checks must be the same session kind; a synthetic first call reads 0 startup tokens and is refused as a reference.

KME-G smoke ranking on GEX44, every figure an upper bound and never a realized saving and never a KME-L result: late rollover 8,773,728.0 (15.98 % of the weighted denominator 54,899,558.8, at or above 3 %, still above 3 % at a growth of 200,000), retries 2,520.6 (0.0046 %), rereads 0.0 (measured zero). The earlier code cherry-pick list was stale (replayed at the frozen commit it leaves the measurement instrument without its frozen-source record), so the laptop items depend on the code sync.

Measured on this history: neither owner ledger carries a terminal for any pillar (a scan printed with_terminal=[] for both at HEAD and at the skill-capability branch), the cognitive-economy phase-1 commit 21671d6c is absent from this clone (git cat-file exits 128), and before this phase the per-pillar done-gate did not run R2 (a J terminal with a misquoted owner terminal printed PASS; fixed and drilled).

Reviewing 16 candidates against the universal knowledge base found one duplicate of an existing entry (rejected) and one sending-side sister of an existing rule (proposed); the only callers of the tower ratchet promote function are tests, so a CBR promotion has no command-line path today and every CBR row is filed against no family; the two performance candidates are on HOLD because the frozen transfer rule needs a second, materially independent workload.
